what_i_see: A red elliptical (likely BCG) with a halo, about 4 arcsec north of the target, surrounded by red cluster members. At the target: a compact reddish galaxy with a faint curved loop or arc about 1 arcsec around it, plus an elongated blue knot about 1 arcsec to its north. Low signal-to-noise.
most_likely: Faint background galaxies (one red, one blue) projected behind a cluster core at z~0.43. The loop may be a tidal or spiral feature, or a blend. Mild cluster lensing distortion is possible.
against_it: The target is 4 arcsec from a catalogued cluster BCG, a plausible strong-lensing radius. The curved faint light could be a lensed arc, but the blue knot looks more radial than tangential.
decisive_test: Deeper or PSF-subtracted VIS imaging, with BCG light modelled out, to check whether the arc is tangential to the BCG with counter-images; or spectroscopy of the arc and knot.
catalogue_notes: LS DR9 REX at 0.1 arcsec: r=23.4, photo-z 1.06 (0.81-1.27), background. BCG (WISEA J100215.69+661836.7, LS photo-z 0.43) at 4.3 arcsec. Wen+2024 cluster J100215.7+661837, z=0.43, M500 0.7e14 Msun, at 4.3 arcsec. Gaia DR3 star G=20.8 at 12 arcsec. Nothing in SIMBAD within 60 arcsec.
